questions.prompt: What money is used in Mexico?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Mexico is the peso.

questions.prompt: True or false: “The capital city of Mexico is Mexico City.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mexico article, or on the Atlas.

questions.proof: The capital city of Mexico is Mexico City.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Mexico about 1,960,647 square kilometres; Finland about 338,478 square kilometres; Guatemala about 108,889 square kilometres; Dominican Republic about 48,671 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Mexico?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People” part of the Mexico article.

questions.proof: Mexico is the most populous Spanish-speaking country in the world.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Mexico?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mexico article.

questions.proof: Mexico City is the capital and largest city, which ranks among the most populous metropolitan areas in the world.
